control_C1_losslessness.name: C1_identity_losslessness
control_C1_losslessness.construction: independent random permutation of all 8960 FFN neurons in ALL 28 layers (seed 20260828); gate/up rows and down columns permuted together, then inverted in place
control_C1_losslessness.expect: BPB unchanged to fp32 summation noise (|dBPB| < 1e-6, i.e. <2e-4 sigma_seed), restore EXACT, max|dlogit| at fp32 round-off relative to logit magnitude
control_C1_losslessness.note: exact bitwise equality is NOT expected and is not the claim: permuting down_proj's columns changes the fp32 summation ORDER.  The claim is that the deviation is round-off, which is why max|dlogit| is reported rather than asserted to be zero.

synthetic_controls.name: C2_planted_positive_coactivation_groups
synthetic_controls.construction: N=8960, T=4096, 64 disjoint contiguous groups of 140 neurons, 6 WHOLE groups active per token, then scrambled by a known permutation (seed 4242)
synthetic_controls.expect: co-activation arm recovers >=90% of the planted skippable AND ARI>0.90, while the identity arm on the scrambled data stays near 0

synthetic_controls.name: C3_planted_negative_iid_matched_density
synthetic_controls.construction: N=8960, T=4096, exactly 896 active/token drawn uniformly
synthetic_controls.expect: all three arms land together on the analytic hypergeometric value; any arm that 'wins' on noise is broken

synthetic_controls.name: C4_random_permutation_invariances
synthetic_controls.why: two shuffle-based nulls on this programme turned out not to be null, and the most recent recovered BETTER than the real arm because the shuffle destroyed a structural constraint and made the problem easier.  So what this shuffle does and does not destroy is stated, then MEASURED, before the arm is trusted.
synthetic_controls.destroyed: ONLY the alignment between neuron index and co-activation
preserved_exactly: the whole co-activation matrix up to relabelling (P^T C P is similar to C: same spectrum, same rank, same clusterability)
synthetic_controls.consequence: the random arm cannot make the problem easier here.  The only quantity it changes is the one the score depends on, and its expectation under a uniform permutation is the exact hypergeometric C(N-k,B)/C(N,B).  C3 checks that expectation is met; a deviation would be an instrument fault, not a finding.
synthetic_controls.expect: all four invariances hold exactly; the shuffle is a null for INDEX ALIGNMENT and for nothing else

synthetic_controls.name: C5_fast_path_equals_D0_layout_stats
synthetic_controls.expect: agreement <1e-12 between this file's index-based accounting and d0_layout.layout_stats, so the memory-lean path inherits D0's own controls

synthetic_controls.name: C6_hypergeometric_reference_vs_monte_carlo
synthetic_controls.expect: closed form matches Monte-Carlo within sampling error (<0.01)

synthetic_controls.name: C7_amendment1_identity_reproduces_brief_table
synthetic_controls.expect: FFN_active=(3-2s)/3 reproduces A1.1's table to 1e-3 and the 2% budget needs s=1.470, which is impossible
